transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer relations. My name is Zack. How can I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Zack. Our home broadband was completely down yesterday afternoon for exactly four hours and twenty minutes between one and five PM! Because of this outage, I was unable to submit bids on a commercial eBay antique auction, causing me to lose a five-hundred-pound profit margin on a rare Georgian mahogany sideboard! I want an immediate five-hundred-pound credit posted to my S-Net billing balance right now on this call, or I will initiate legal action against your company in small claims court!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me open your subscriber ledger and service history records on our billing portal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My S-Net account number is ACC-88910-L.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we inspect the service outage logs, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The installation address is 52 Claremont Road, Manchester, M14 5WP, and the security PIN is 6620.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Luke. I have opened your Manchester account docket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are requesting: you experienced a service outage of four hours yesterday afternoon, and you are seeking five hundred pounds in direct financial compensation for lost speculative antique auction profits. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly! Five hundred pounds of clear financial loss caused entirely by your network dropping out in the middle of a live auction!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please hold for about forty-five seconds while I review the regional network incident logs and our standard compensation matrix.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Luke. Network operations logs confirm that an overhead street cabinet power failure affected your neighborhood yesterday for four hours and twenty minutes before backup generators restored mains power to the line cards.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So S-Net admits full liability for the outage! Process the five-hundred-pound credit right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the Ofcom Automatic Compensation Scheme, residential broadband subscribers are entitled to statutory compensation only when a complete loss of service persists beyond two full working days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Two full working days?! I don't care about your statutory schemes! I lost five hundred pounds in cold hard cash yesterday afternoon!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Section 14.2 of our Consumer Broadband Agreement explicitly excludes indirect consequential economic damages or lost commercial profits resulting from temporary residential service disruptions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Your terms and conditions are completely irrelevant to me! I demand to speak to a senior director who has check-signing authority!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Senior executive directors do not handle frontline inbound customer telephone queues.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then you credit my account five hundred pounds right now or I will post negative reviews across every consumer trust website and drag your name through the mud!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The maximum goodwill credit a frontline team member can authorize for a single-day residential outage is ten pounds under company guidelines.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ten pounds?! Are you insulting my intelligence?! Ten pounds is a slap in the face! I want five hundred pounds, not a pathetic ten-pound voucher!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Well Luke, if you think S-Net is handing out five hundred pounds of free money for a four-hour residential outage, you can get lost because that is never going to happen!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did you just tell me to get lost?! You told a paying customer to get lost on a recorded call?! That is unbelievable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the commercial reality that five hundred pounds of compensation will not be approved under any circumstances for a residential contract, as set out in our regulatory code of practice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am recording this call and sending it straight to BBC Watchdog, Trading Standards, and the communications ombudsman!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm what you mentioned earlier, your registered S-Net account number is ACC-88910-L?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, ACC-88910-L. You will see that number on the formal legal writ my solicitor files!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What was the specific category of antique goods you were bidding on when the connection dropped?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It was a set of Victorian mahogany dining chairs and a Georgian silver tea service being auctioned in an online timed catalog.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you attempt to access the online auction platform using a mobile telephone cellular connection during the outage?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My mobile phone battery was at four percent and charging in another room, so I didn't think of switching over in time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Had mobile hotspot tethering been utilized, the auction portal would have remained accessible over 4G cellular data.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I pay S-Net for fixed broadband so that I don't have to fiddle with tiny smartphone screens!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Fixed broadband infrastructure remains subject to utility power grid interruptions beyond provider control.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Commercial leased lines with four-hour SLAs cost hundreds of pounds, but you advertise ninety-nine percent reliability!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Ninety-nine percent annual availability still allows for several hours of unscheduled maintenance or environmental power cuts over twelve months.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you are refusing to give me a single penny more than ten pounds?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under the Consumer Broadband Code of Practice, frontline authorization limits for non-extended service outages are strictly bounded at ten pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What about my legal rights under the Consumer Rights Act 2015 for services not provided with reasonable care and skill?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Any formal statutory claim alleging breach of implied terms under the Consumer Rights Act must be submitted in writing to our legal compliance directorate in Leeds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will have my legal counsel draft that formal claim letter by registered delivery tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If our customer relations team cannot reach a mutual agreement with you within eight weeks, we will issue a formal Deadlock Notice enabling you to refer the case to CISAS.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: CISAS is the Communications and Internet Services Adjudication Scheme, which costs your company hundreds of pounds per adjudication!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, CISAS is our designated independent alternative dispute resolution body approved by Ofcom.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will take this all the way to CISAS adjudication unless an executive manager calls me back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have documented your compensation claim on the ticket and logged the maximum ten-pound goodwill adjustment against next month's invoice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am rejecting your ten-pound offer and will pursue this through legal channels.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The formal dispute reference number for your complaint docket is DIS-44019-L.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Noted down... DIS-44019-L.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The dispute notes clearly state your demand for five hundred pounds and our residential terms limitation.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Our mobile phone network with S-Net has always had excellent 5G signal across Manchester, we get full bars everywhere in Rusholme and Fallowfield, so mobile service is fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: We are pleased that your Manchester cellular coverage maintains strong performance across Greater Manchester.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, the mobile coverage has been fine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ten-pound adjustment and formal dispute documentation are locked on your profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will be expecting written confirmation of this dispute docket by post.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A formal written summary detailing our final dispute response will be dispatched to your registered billing address within five working days by recorded delivery.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Very well.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have verified that your dispute docket DIS-44019-L is submitted and your ten-pound credit is noted. Does that answer all of your questions regarding the claim process today, Luke?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You haven't paid me what you owe me, but you've explained the claim process. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Have a good afternoon. Goodbye Luke.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
